findings.source_quote: εἶτα ἐπιθυμία πράξεων πολλῶν καὶ πολυτέλεια ἐδεσμάτων πολλῶν καὶ μεθυσμάτων καὶ κραιπαλῶν πολλῶν
findings.english_quote: Then come cravings for many undertakings, costly foods and intoxicating drinks, many revelries
findings.issue: The simplified wording no longer explicitly renders πολυτέλεια, extravagance or luxurious expenditure/consumption, as a vice. Costly foods are not equivalent to extravagance in foods and drinks. It also omits πολλῶν modifying foods. Unlike the standard edition, the simplified list can consequently be read as listing foods and drinks themselves, or merely craving them, rather than the specified extravagance.
findings.suggested_revision: For fresh review: “Then come cravings for many undertakings, extravagance in many foods and intoxicating drinks, many revelries”. Preserve both the extravagance and the quantity attached to foods.

findings.source_quote: πρῶτον πάντων ὀξύχολός ἐστι καὶ πικρὸς καὶ ἄφρων
findings.english_quote: He is quick-tempered, bitter and senseless.
findings.issue: The simplified edition omits πρῶτον πάντων, “first of all,” which explicitly orders or foregrounds these identifying characteristics before the subsequent account of the angel’s works.
findings.suggested_revision: For fresh review: “First of all, he is quick-tempered, bitter and senseless.”

findings.source_quote: εἶτα ἐπιθυμία πράξεων πολλῶν καὶ πολυτέλεια ἐδεσμάτων πολλῶν καὶ μεθυσμάτων καὶ κραιπαλῶν πολλῶν
findings.english_quote: The complete Greek vice list is retained, including luxuries of various kinds AND things that are not fitting, preserving the earlier grammatical decision.
findings.issue: In the simplified edition, footnote f overstates fidelity by claiming that the complete Greek vice list is retained. Although the luxuries/not-fitting distinction is preserved, the main text loses the explicit extravagance item and the qualification “many” attached to foods.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore the missing source content in the simplified main text and review this completeness claim again. If the current wording remains, the note must disclose its reduction rather than claim complete retention.

summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against the complete selected Greek. The standard edition is acceptable against that working source. The simplified edition needs correction in II.4–5 and a corresponding check of footnote f. Both preserve the bracketed editorial material, whole-heart turning to the Lord, servant terminology, speaker distinctions, negations, and both necessity assertions. The textual notes are otherwise compatible with the supplied bounded project reports; this review does not authenticate unseen editions, manuscript images, handwriting, or exhaustive collation. Proposed corrections require fresh review.
